_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH)

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized (1:1), open-label, multicenter, active-controlled, non-inferiority study versus eculizumab
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with PNH (at least 5% PNH cells) who were naïve to complement inhibitor treatment
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Coprimary endpoints: transfusion avoidance (TA) and hemolysis measured by LDH normalization (LDH-N)
pivotal_trials.result: Non-inferiority demonstrated. Transfusion avoidance 73.6% (ULTOMIRIS) vs 66.1% (eculizumab), difference 6.8% (95% CI: -4.66, 18.14); LDH normalization 53.6% vs 49.4%, odds ratio 1.19 (95% CI: 0.80, 1.77).

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized (1:1), open-label, multicenter, active-controlled, non-inferiority study; patients continued eculizumab or switched to ULTOMIRIS
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with PNH who were clinically stable after treatment with eculizumab for at least the previous 6 months
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: hemolysis as directly measured by percent change in LDH from baseline to Day 183
pivotal_trials.result: Non-inferiority demonstrated. LDH percent change -0.82% (ULTOMIRIS) vs 8.4% (eculizumab), difference 9.2% (95% CI: -0.42, 18.8).

key_safety: Most common TEAEs (>10%) in ULTOMIRIS patients: upper respiratory tract infections (39%) and headache (32.0%). Serious adverse reactions in 15 (6.8%) patients; most serious risk is life-threatening meningococcal infections/sepsis.
target_moa: Recombinant humanized monoclonal antibody that binds the human C5 complement protein and inhibits its cleavage to C5a and C5b, preventing generation of the terminal complement complex C5b-9

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: SERIOUS MENINGOCOCCAL INFECTIONS — life-threatening meningococcal infections/sepsis have occurred and may become rapidly life-threatening or fatal if not recognized and treated early

rems.type: A REMS is required for ULTOMIRIS to ensure the benefits outweigh the risk of meningococcal infection

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected for a biologic of this class in the intended population

description.text: Added new indication for treatment of adults and pediatric patients one month and older with atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) to inhibit complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for a new indication for the treatment of adults and pediatric patients one month of age and older with atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) to inhibit complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA). This supplement also provides for proposed modifications to the REMS related to the new indication.

description.text: Added a new 100 mg/mL concentration with 300 mg/3 mL and 1100 mg/11 mL vial presentations for adult PNH patients

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for a new concentration, 100 mg/mL, with two vial presentations: 300 mg/3 mL and 1100 mg/11 mL, for the treatment of adult patients with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH).

description.text: Expanded to include treatment of pediatric patients with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for the treatment of pediatric patients with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH).

description.text: Added a new subcutaneous route of administration (on-body delivery system) for adult patients with PNH and aHUS

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for adding a new route of administration for Ultomiris via subcutaneous injection for the treatment of adult patients with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH) and atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS), and a new dosage form and strength, the Ultomiris 70mg/mL, 3.5 mL on-body delivery system. This supplement also provides for modifications to the approved Ultomiris risk evaluation and mitigation strategy (REMS).

description.text: Added indication for treatment of adult patients with generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) who are anti-AChR antibody-positive

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for the treatment of adult patients with generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody-positive and proposed modifications to the approved Ultomiris REMS.

description.text: Added new indication for treatment of adult patients with NMOSD who are anti-aquaporin-4 (AQP4) antibody positive

citations.quote: Prior Approval sBLA S-26 provides for a new indication for the treatment of adult patients with neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) who are anti-aquaporin-4 (AQP4) antibody positive and proposed modifications to the approved Ultomiris REMS. In addition, Prior Approval sBLA S-31 provides for proposed modifications to the approved Ultomiris REMS to form a combined REMS with Soliris. This supplement is in response, in part, to our May 16, 2023, REMS Modification Notification Letter.

orphan_indication.text: Ravulizumab has orphan drug designation for the sought PNH indication (application exempt from PREA)

citations.quote: This application is exempt from the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA) requirements because ravulizumab has orphan drug designation for the sought indication.

basis.text: The BLA received priority review designation

summary.text: ULTOMIRIS received regular (full) approval under priority review for the treatment of adult patients with PNH, based on two non-inferiority trials versus eculizumab; the product has orphan drug designation for the PNH indication and a REMS is required for meningococcal infection risk.

citations.quote: The review teams recommend regular approval of ULTOMIRIS (ravulizumab-cwvz) under 21 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 601 for the indication, “treatment of adult patients with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria”.
This application is exempt from the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA) requirements because ravulizumab has orphan drug designation for the sought indication.
